$comment: Gate 1 (devolt memory/decisions/2026-09-25-brownout-core-w1-plan.md, section
3.4.1; core/README.md's contract). Every test case in every suite file
wired into vitest.core-suites.config.ts's `test.include` is listed here,
classified as one of:
- "portable":     runs on the core for the kinds it uses; wired into
vitest.core-suites.config.ts's testNamePattern.
- "classic-only":  pins a classic-internal detail (step counts, Newton
iteration counts, engine.state, captureErrorState,
a split) that has no core counterpart and is not
part of the accuracy contract; never runs on the core.
- "not-yet":       every kind the test's circuit uses is real device
behaviour, but at least one of those kinds has not
been ported to the core yet (or, for a handful of
kinds below, is not in the W1 plan's kind table at
all -- diode/bjt_npn/nmos/lm358/microbit).
`kinds` lists every SimComponent.kind the test's circuit instantiates
(excluding the implicit ground net). gate-reporter.ts sums, per kind, how
many "portable" cases actually ran and passed under this file's
testNamePattern, and fails the whole run if any kind named in a portable
case's `kinds` array has a count of zero for that file -- see its own
header comment for why this must be computed from portable entries only,
not from CORE_IMPLEMENTED_KINDS (which also contains "ground", a compiler-
internal detail no test ever names as a component kind). It ALSO fails
when any CORE_IMPLEMENTED_KINDS member except "ground" has no portable
case, in any file, that ran and passed (the coverage floor, W1b review
finding 9): a kind the core implements must be exercised here.
W1e added suite files that mix cases of every kind and listed only the cases that build one of the six W1e kinds (led, rgb_led,
bicolor_led, seg7_cc, seg7_ca, ne555). G-0's verifier closed that: every case of every listed file now has exactly one row (146 rows added to 14 files,
among them wave2-*, wave3-*, wave5-*, ac-*, arduino, environment, hcsr04 and extended-integration), and classification-totals.test.ts fails when a case has no row.

W1f added battery-engine-physics.test.ts and the bench_psu cases of wave5-regulators.test.ts (its regulator cases are W3 and unlisted), reclassified the eleven not-yet cases its kinds unblocked, and added waveform-sources-supplemental.test.ts for clock_gen, pulse_gen and pulse_source, which no classic suite builds from implemented kinds alone. digital-pulse.test.ts and waveform.test.ts build no circuit (they test classic's waveform functions directly), so they have nothing to run on the core and are not wired in.

W1g (G4) wired in led-damage-limit-irated, wave3-protection's ptc_fuse cases, the 0.6.1 fixes' own tests (output-sag-direction, resistor-default-overload, thermal-cold-start-warnings, ls47-released-segment-sag) and engine-warnings, reclassified failure-states, thermal-engine-physics and catalog-identity (W1g point 19.3), and moved the four rows that cited the removed led-thermal decline. A case that reloads mid-failure, or needs saveState, is W2 (W1g point 15, Q8); the op-amp, 7805, lm393 and transistor cases are W3; missing_flyback moves to W3 (W1g round 2 ruling): every case switches its winding with a W3 transistor.

W2i reclassified the cases W2 unblocked (W2 design section 6). eeprom-write's fifteen went with W2c piece 5 (578a518). The other thirteen went here: the ten that reload and need the carry (the four 74HC14 dead-band cases and the 74ls47 delay case in wave2-combinational, the two 74HC74 capture cases in wave2-sequential, battery's warm load, failure-states' failed-open branch and wave3-protection's PTC recovery) and the three that need the snapshot (battery's rollback, thermal's rollback, extended-integration's 555 chaser, for which the adapter's saveState() returns the published readouts too). step-breakpoints' four are classic-only by ruling D18 (a). What stays not-yet waits for a kind: W1h (cd4511, cd4017, cd4060, 74hc595, potentiometer and the other unported kinds), W3 (the analog parts) or W6 (DC-OP and small-signal AC). wave5-regulators' two 'first accepted step' cases read classic's saveState().failureStress map, which the core's snapshot does not expose, and stay not-yet as they were (they were not among the 28).

PSU-2 (ruling R116 (2), the decline-only cut) wired in psu-sink-limit.test.ts, the classic bench supply's sources-only cases (c98bf73, f6418c1). The core models no let-go: a supply it would see sink more than 1 uA declines with bench-psu-back-driven, so no case runs on the core here. Each runs through HeadlessRunner's auto mode instead, its fallback reason and classic's answer pinned, in test/host/psu-sink-limit-auto.test.ts.

G-0 (gate scaffolding, plan 1.0.0 row G-0) classified the 91 test files this file did not list yet (140 files outside test/core, 49 listed before). A file with at least one "portable" case is listed under `suites` with every one of its cases, exactly like the files above, so the core-suites project collects it and runs the portable ones. A file with no portable case is listed under `unwired` instead: same rows, but the core-suites project never collects it (a mass of files that fall back or pin classic internals would only slow the gate down). `test/core/suites/classification-totals.test.ts` fails when a test file is in neither list, so an unclassified new test file fails the suite.

Every row of both lists has `kinds` and `reason`. A "not-yet" row also names `package` (the package of the plan whose landing lets it run: the last of its `blockedBy` to land, in the order of PACKAGE_ORDER in classification-totals.ts) and `blockedBy` (every package it waits for). A "classic-only" row names its `disposition`: "classic-internal" (pins a classic detail with no core counterpart), "engine-independent" (builds no circuit of a device kind; nothing to run), or "host-selects-engine" (drives HeadlessRunner, an analysis driver or the part library, which pick their own engine). `pnpm run classification:totals` prints the per-package table.

Cases whose title is generated (it.each, template strings) are listed once per generated name, as vitest reports it; a name that repeats in a file is listed once with `count`. The kinds of a portable case were recorded from the circuits it loaded through the adapter; the kinds of the others come from the case's code and the circuits it loaded before it stopped, and over-approximate (a case can be called "not-yet" for a kind its assertions merely name, never "portable" wrongly).

cases.describe: reference physics — transient KCL/KVL and energy residuals
cases.name: RC companion satisfies KCL and its discrete energy identity
cases.reason: Reconstructs `capacitorCurrent = capacitance * (voltage - previousVoltage) / h` and checks a KCL residual against it -- a property of classic's own fixed-h backward-Euler finite difference, not of the device's continuous physics. The core's single-capacitor partition (W1b step 2) advances the closed form continuously (no per-step h to reconstruct a matching discrete derivative from), so this identity is not a like-for-like comparison there. Forcing the core's generic stepped path (FORCE_STEPPED, core/README.md's Options table) would make the two arithmetically comparable again -- but the gate-1 adapter (test/core/suites/adapter.ts) is built on HeadlessRunner, and HeadlessRunnerOptions/HeadlessRunOptions carry no compile-options passthrough (no forceStepped, no CompileOptions of any kind) -- so there is currently no way to route this specific case's assertion onto the core's stepped path through this harness. A future worker could add that passthrough (HeadlessRunnerOptions.compileOptions, threaded into CoreEngine.load's options) to lift this to "portable" under FORCE_STEPPED.

cases.describe: spdt_switch.updateCurrent — Q-O26 (com to the contact in use)
cases.name: position 0 (com->b active, b floating with no load) reports ~0 A: no complete circuit
cases.reason: com is fixed (wired directly to the source) and b is the device's only OTHER free pin (c has no wire to it either in this case's own rig, since r1 sits on c) -- wait, r1 is wired to c even here, so b and c are the device's two free contacts in potentially different partitions (com fixed, so nothing unions them, per finding 1). The ACTIVE contact at position 0 is com-b, and b's own partition IS the device's attributed owner (owner_of picks the first free pin among [com,b,c] in declared order, i.e. b) -- so this reads the owning partition's own contact, not a cross-partition one, and is unaffected by finding 1's cross-partition mis-stamp.

cases.reason: com fixed; b and c are two DIFFERENT free-node partitions (b isolated, c loaded through r1) with the device's Owner attributed to b (the first free pin), exactly finding 1's cross-partition scenario -- but this circuit has no capacitor anywhere, so both partitions are Static, and the static solver evidently solves the whole static graph as one combined system rather than per-partition with local indexing (finding 1's fixed[node].unwrap_or(0.0) fabrication is specific to the dynamic ClosedForm/Stepped compile_dyn_shape path). Verified empirically against the built core: this reports the correct ~5 mA, not a fabricated-0V-driven phantom current.

cases.name: stamps leakage as an actual terminal shunt
cases.reason: Plain resistor+capacitor(esr, leakageResistance) DC-settled divider, read through engine.nets/getNetV/getElementI only -- no classic-internal calls. CORE_RECORD_SHAPES.capacitor's 3 params (capacitance, esr, leakage) cover both non-default fields this fixture sets.

cases.name: applies exact catalog ESR/leakage defaults to an older identified save
cases.reason: This fixture's capacitor sits directly across the ideal source (c.a to src.pos, c.b to src.neg) -- BOTH terminals are fixed nodes, and rule 2a (core/README.md) now gives the core an exact closed form for exactly this topology instead of declining it, so the old topology block is gone. But this specific test is not a rule-2a check: it hand-computes ONE deliberately huge backward-Euler step (h=0.5s against esr=1, C=1F -- h/(esr*C) = 0.5, half of tau) and asserts classic's OWN single-step companion value, series 5/(1+0.5/1) = 3.3333333333333335 A plus leakage 5/1e7 = 5e-7 A, total 3.3333338333333336 A. Verified empirically by temporarily marking this case portable: the core reports the mathematically exact rule-2a answer instead -- series 5*exp(-0.5) = 3.0326532985631669 A plus the same 5e-7 A leakage, total 3.032653798563167 A (bit-identical to `fixedPairCapacitorCurrentAt(5, 1, 1, 1e7, 0.5)`, test/core/equivalence/analytic.ts) -- which differs from classic's crude one-step approximation by 0.30068 A, about 9% of the expected value and six orders of magnitude past this test's 5e-8 `toBeCloseTo` bound. This is not the load-instant/first-step artifact rule 2a's README bullet documents (that is specific to esr=0); it is classic's own large-step discretisation error at a genuinely non-ideal esr, which the core is BY DESIGN more accurate than. Reclassifying this exact assertion portable would require either the core to reproduce classic's inexact single-step arithmetic (wrong direction for W1b) or loosening this test's own tolerance (which this worker does not own and must not do to force a pass) -- so it stays classic-only, for a materially different reason than before.

cases.describe: spst switch — closed and open contacts
cases.name: a closed contact is 1 mOhm: the load sees the supply less the contact drop, and the switch reports the series current
cases.reason: Plain SPST switch (switch, the kind no other gate-1 suite exercises) in series with a resistor off an ideal source, read only through nets/getNetV/getElementI after step(). The closed contact is the same literal 1 mOhm on both engines (core/README.md's switch row), so the divider and the contact current match.

cases.describe: spst switch — closed and open contacts
cases.name: an open contact stamps nothing: the load node falls to 0 V and the switch reports 0 A
cases.reason: Plain SPST switch (switch, the kind no other gate-1 suite exercises) in series with a resistor off an ideal source, read only through nets/getNetV/getElementI after step(). An open contact stamps nothing on either engine; the load node sits on r1 and the node shunt, and the switch publishes 0.

cases.describe: spst switch — closed and open contacts
cases.name: the string "0" counts as closed, because classic reads the param with Boolean()
cases.reason: Plain SPST switch (switch, the kind no other gate-1 suite exercises) in series with a resistor off an ideal source, read only through nets/getNetV/getElementI after step(). The compiler resolves closed with the same Boolean() rule (core/README.md: the string "0" counts as closed), so the core closes the contact too.

cases.name: reloading with the contact opened after it was closed drops the load to 0 V
cases.reason: A carry-forward reload with the contact toggled open; the adapter's load() reloads the core program with time carried, as HeadlessRunner does for classic.

cases.name: a closed contact charges a capacitor behind it toward the supply, and an open one never does
cases.reason: A switch-gated RC: closed, the capacitor charges through 1 mOhm (tau about 1 ns) in a closed-form partition; open, the node never moves. Exercises a switch stamp inside a dynamic partition.

cases.name: output is LOW when input is above V_T+ (5V supply)
cases.reason: Powered 74HC14 Schmitt inverter with a pull-up on the output, read only through engine.nets/getNetV after step() — exercises core/README.md digital-core rules 1 (thresholds from live rails) and 8 (output stage). No classic-internal call.

cases.name: output is HIGH when input is below V_T- (5V supply)
cases.reason: Same rig as the LOW case, input below V_T-; see that case's reason.

cases.name: holds LOW output when input is in dead band approached from above
cases.reason: W2i: portable since W2c's load carry-forward (core/README.md, Carry). The reload carries the 74HC14's per-input Schmitt level by component id, so the dead-band input keeps the output LOW. It failed before the carry (the output flipped on the reload) and passes on the built core now.

cases.name: holds HIGH output when input is in dead band approached from below
cases.reason: W2i: portable since W2c's load carry-forward (core/README.md, Carry). It used to pass only because a reloaded Schmitt input started LOW; the carried level is what holds the output HIGH now, and the 'approached from above' sibling, which the old default could not pass, proves the carry.

cases.name: thresholds scale with a 3V supply (V_T+ ~1.62V, V_T- ~0.96V)
cases.reason: Confirms core/README.md rule 4's Schmitt scale factor s = vS/nominal at a non-5V supply; plain load()/step()/getNetV, no classic-internal call.

cases.name: digit 6: top bar (segment a) is RELEASED — classic LS47, no top bar
cases.reason: Datasheet-specific partial glyph for digit 6 (no segment a), distinguishing the real 74LS47 table from a generic hex decoder; same rig as the full sweep above.

cases.name: digit 6: segment b is RELEASED — classic LS47 partial six
cases.reason: Same digit-6 partial glyph, segment b; see the segment-a case's reason.

cases.name: digit 9: bottom bar (segment d) is RELEASED — classic LS47, no bottom
cases.reason: Datasheet-specific partial glyph for digit 9 (no segment d); same rig as the full sweep.

cases.name: forces all seven segment outputs LOW when /LT is asserted (LOW)
cases.reason: Lamp-test override forces every segment to sink regardless of the BCD input (core/README.md rule 7's lt_n precedence over the BCD decode); plain load()/step()/getNetV.

cases.name: releases all outputs when /RBO is driven LOW externally (blanking input)
cases.reason: /RBO driven LOW releases every segment, but BCD=15 (a=b=c=d=HIGH) is already blank (LS47_SEGMENTS[15]) — a core that ignored rbo_n entirely and always fell through to the BCD decode would pass this case unnoticed. It only proves rbo_n does not break the already-blank case, not that it takes precedence over a real decode. The genuine precedence check (a non-blank BCD forced blank by rbo_n LOW, plus a same-BCD control with rbo_n HIGH) is combinational-ics.test.ts's "gate 1 supplemental — 74LS47 /RBO blanking precedence" describe block (review finding 15).

cases.name: zero-suppresses digit 0 when /RBI is LOW
cases.reason: Ripple-blanking input on BCD=0 releases every segment (zero suppression); plain load()/step()/getNetV.

cases.name: decodes BCD digit 5 normally when /LT, /RBI, /RBO are all left unconnected
cases.reason: /LT, /RBI and /RBO left OPEN must resolve HIGH (core/README.md rule 4's OPEN_HIGH pins, IC_OPEN_HIGH_PINS) so the chip decodes normally instead of latching lamp-test or blanking; exercises the open-pin path distinct from the floating-input path (those three pins are OPEN_HIGH, not FLOATING_INPUT).

cases.name: dead-band input from above: output stays LOW across 20 steps
cases.reason: W2i: portable since W2c's load carry-forward (core/README.md, Carry). Same carried Schmitt level as the 'approached from above' case; failed before the carry, passes on the built core now.

cases.name: dead-band input from below: output stays HIGH across 20 steps
cases.reason: W2i: portable since W2c's load carry-forward (core/README.md, Carry). Same as the 'approached from below' case: the carried Schmitt level holds the output, not the reload default; its 'from above' sibling proves the carry.

cases.reason: Pure local-function formula check (expectedThresholds()) duplicating classic's module-private thresholdsFor (sim-engine.ts) -- never constructs a SimCircuit or SimEngine, so nothing here is routed through the adapter or exercises the core at all; alias-agnostic, not a core proof.

cases.name: CMOS-4000 and HC-CMOS use the same 0.3/0.7 ratios at 5V
cases.reason: Same pure-formula check as the 5V case; see its reason.

cases.name: 74ls08 uses prefix fallback of 20ns (no prop_delay_ns in catalog)
cases.reason: Weak assertion (engine.digitalState['u1/1y'] is defined) after one large step on a powered 74ls08 AND gate; exercises load()/step()/digitalState for the one kind (74ls08) no other case in this file's sweeps names. Does not itself pin the 20 ns delay value (that is classic's own catalog-fallback resolution, consumed identically by the core's own delay param per core/README.md's IC blob per-pin delay field) — and, being merely "defined", it cannot distinguish AND from NAND, OR, or any other committed 2-input function either (review finding 14). The real truth-table proof (both LOW, one HIGH, and — the row that actually distinguishes AND from NAND — both HIGH) is combinational-ics.test.ts's "gate 1 supplemental — 74LS08 quad AND" describe block; this case is left as-is because its own subject (the prop-delay prefix fallback) is unaffected by that gap.

cases.name: 74hc595 uses prefix fallback of 15ns (no prop_delay_ns in catalog)
cases.reason: 74hc595 is W1d/W1h (shift register); not implemented by the core yet.

cases.name: 74hc14 uses catalog-declared prop_delay_ns=15 (same value as prefix default)
cases.reason: Loads with the input already at its final level, so the load-time settle (zero delay, core/README.md's events section: "the first observation has zero delay") resolves 1y before any delay could ever be observed — a catalog delay of 0 ns, 15 ns or 50 us would all pass this case identically (sampled after two 100 us steps, far past any of them). This only proves the gate inverts (the input/output pin mapping and polarity are correct), never that any particular propagation delay is honoured. The genuine observable-delay check (a continuous RC threshold crossing during ordinary step()s, never a reload) is combinational-ics.test.ts's "gate 1 supplemental — 74HC14 Schmitt inverter: a genuinely observed propagation delay" case (review finding 15).

cases.name: 74ls47 uses catalog-declared prop_delay_ns=35 — output delay observable
cases.reason: W2i: portable since W2c's load carry-forward (core/README.md, Carry). The reload that changes the BCD input carries the 74ls47's committed outputs, so the new value is an ordinary transition that waits the catalog's 35 ns, and 25 ns after the reload digitalState still shows the old one. It failed before the carry (a reload was a first observation with zero delay).

cases.name: leaves an unpowered 74LS00 output to the external bias network instead of publishing a driven digital state
cases.reason: The 74LS00's vcc/gnd pins are left entirely unwired (OPEN), so core/README.md rule 1 (powered = false when a supply pin is OPEN) must leave the IC unpowered: no digitalState entry, and the output node floats to whatever the external resistor divider sets it to. Exercises rules 1, 8 and 9 (power gate, output stage, power loss) with no classic-internal call.

cases.name: leaves an unpowered 74HC595 output to the external bias network instead of publishing a driven digital state
cases.reason: 74hc595 is W1d/W1h (shift register); not implemented by the core yet.

cases.name: treats 74LS inputs as TTL-level high by 3 V and low below the 0.8 V band
cases.reason: Two powered 74LS00 runs at different input voltages, read only through getNetV after step(); exercises core/README.md rule 4's TTL fixed vil/vih thresholds (not the CMOS ratio path 74hc14/74hc138 exercise elsewhere in this suite).

cases.name: keeps a 74HC595 input at 3 V below the 5 V supply-aware high threshold
cases.reason: 74hc595 is W1d/W1h; not implemented by the core yet.

cases.name: returns the same seeded result across loads, and the floating input sits above an ideal grounded low
cases.reason: The u1:1b open-input golden vector decision 9 names explicitly (core/README.md rule 5-6, the W1 plan's decision 9: 'the corpus has open-input cases, such as the u1:1b golden vector, digital-realism.test.ts:605-621'). Two independent classic-style runs of the SAME floating circuit must agree with each other (the FNV-1a hash is a pure function of id:pin:bucket, not of engine identity or call order), and must differ from a hard-grounded reference. Verified empirically against the built core (see this worker's report) rather than assumed from the spec text alone.

cases.name: holds a 74LS gate output until the package delay has elapsed
cases.reason: After engine.load(circuit), this mutates circuit.components.find(...).params.voltage on the SAME retained JS object WITHOUT calling engine.load() again, relying on classic's load() keeping a live reference (this.circuit = circuit, sim-engine.ts:2445) and re-reading component.params on every subsequent Newton iterate. The core adapter's load() compiles the circuit into a WASM program once; a later in-place mutation of the JS object has no effect on an already-loaded core program (there is no live binding, and Decision 1's toggle mechanism covers only switch/dip 'closed' params, not a voltage_source's voltage). Routing this case through the core would silently keep the OLD input forever and fail its own later assertion (digitalState flipping after the delay) rather than reproduce classic's propagation-delay behaviour — a classic implementation-detail dependency, not a like-for-like core comparison. (The core's own delay-FSM timing is instead proven by the 74ls47 prop_delay_ns case above, which DOES reload.)

cases.name: reports output-conflict when two push-pull outputs share a net
cases.reason: Calls runDiagnostics() over a plain Circuit/nets pair (buildNets, the diagnostics module) — no SimCircuit, no SimEngine, nothing the core-suites adapter could intercept. Pure topology diagnostics, not a physics comparison.

cases.name: opens an overloaded resistor and reset restores runtime conduction
cases.reason: W1g: runs on the core and passes. 10 ohm across 5 V (2.5 W against the 0.25 W default rating) latches resistor_overload (W1g point 6), the failed resistor reads 0 A (point 12), and the adapter's resetFailures (CoreEngine, point 13) restores conduction at once.

cases.name: removes a failed-open branch instead of coupling high-impedance nodes through 1 GΩ
cases.reason: W2i: portable since W2c's load carry-forward (core/README.md, Carry). The mid-failure reload carries the latched resistor_overload and the open branch by id and kind, as classic's does. It failed before the carry with 'expected [] to deeply equal [ resistor_overload ]'.

cases.name: checks potentiometer wiper-segment power instead of end-to-end current
cases.reason: Ran and passed on the core through the gate-1 adapter (P0-SG).

cases.name: fails an overloaded resistor-array channel independently
cases.reason: Ran and passed on the core through the gate-1 adapter (P0-SG).

cases.name: trips a fuse open and clears it with resetFailures
cases.reason: W1g: runs on the core and passes. 0.1 ohm across 5 V is 50 A through a 0.5 A fuse: fuse_tripped latches (W1g point 8), the open fuse reads 0 A, and resetFailures clears the set.

cases.name: uses a magnitude-dependent fuse I-squared-t curve
cases.reason: W1g: runs on the core and passes. At 1.05x the rate (1.05^2 - 1 = 0.1025/s) never reaches 0.3 in 2 s; at 10x it trips before 2x (W1g point 8's analytic latch times).

cases.name: fails an overcurrent LED without persisting burnt params
cases.reason: W1g: runs on the core and passes. A red LED (no uid) on 25 ohm from 5 V latches led_failed (W1g point 7), reads 0 A afterwards, never writes params.burnt, and resetFailures clears it.

cases.name: treats IC brownout as a recoverable operating condition, not permanent damage
cases.reason: A 3 V supply leaves the 74LS00 below core/README.md rule 1's 0.9*vccMin power window (unpowered, no failures published — trivially true on the core too, since W1g's failure machinery has not landed and getFailures() returns {} regardless); reloading at 5 V (a genuine engine.load() call, not the live-mutation-without-reload pattern the propagation-delay case above relies on) must recover the SAME chip with no manual reset and drive the NAND output HIGH. Exercises rule 9 (power loss / recovery) end to end. Verified empirically against the built core.

cases.name: reports loaded digital-output sag as a reversible warning without degrading the driver
cases.reason: W1g: runs on the core and passes. 1Y into 100 ohm latches output_sag on 1y (W1g point 9) without touching the stamp; the reload with 10 kohm starts fresh on the core (point 15) and the pin is back above 4 V.

cases.name: debounces output sag so a single-step switching transient never surfaces
cases.reason: W1g: runs on the core and passes. At load the sag is Pending from START_TIME and unpublished; it latches 1e-8 s later (OUTPUT_SAG_WINDOW, W1g point 9), inside the case's first 1 ms step.

cases.reason: New case (this worker); the mux's other select state. See the SELECT-LOW case's reason on /OE scope.

cases.reason: New case (this worker; owner decision 3, Q-O64). The real SN74LS157's /G HIGH forces every Y LOW; A=B=5V and 1y on the file's own pull-up shows the strobe overriding both SELECT and the data, not merely releasing the bus. Both engines now agree here — classic's own /oe-HIGH evaluator branch (digital.ts:499) is reachable now, not dead code.

cases.reason: New case (this worker; no pre-existing classic suite builds a real 74ls245 circuit — see this file's own header comment). Only the well-established DIR=A->B, /OE-LOW path is exercised here; /OE-disabled release and bus contention between two 245s are NOT yet covered by a harness fixture — the /OE-toggle harness fixtures (21-23) are a later worker's (D4), not asserted here by hand.

cases.name: DIR=A->B, /OE enabled: a LOW A1 actively pulls B1 LOW against its own pull-up (only a genuinely driving 245 can do this)
cases.reason: Review finding 14: the pre-existing HIGH-A1 case cannot falsify a reversed DIR (B->A) or a disabled /OE, since b1 sits on a pull-up to vcc through r_out and reads ~5V either way. A LOW result can only come from the 245 actively pulling b1 down against that same pull-up — the one polarity that genuinely exercises DIR/OE.

cases.reason: New case (this worker; no pre-existing classic suite builds a real 74ls283 circuit — see this file's own header comment). A plain 4-bit addition with no carry propagation past bit 3.

cases.name: 15 + 1 + c0=0 = 16 (binary 10000): sum wraps to 0000 with carry out
cases.reason: New case (this worker); exercises the full ripple-carry chain (every internal carry set) and the c4 carry-out pin.

cases.name: gate 1 with one input HIGH (the other LOW) drives the output LOW
cases.reason: New case (review finding 14); AND truth table's mixed-input row — rules out an OR-flavoured implementation together with the both-HIGH case below.

cases.name: gate 1 with both inputs HIGH drives the output HIGH (distinguishes AND from NAND/OR)
cases.reason: New case (review finding 14); the one row that actually distinguishes AND from NAND (which would give LOW here) — exactly the gap the pre-existing wave2-combinational.test.ts 74ls08 case (a bare toBeDefined() check) could not close.

cases.name: BCD=5 (non-blank) with rbo_n driven LOW still releases every segment — /RBO overrides the normal decode, not just a digit that was already blank
cases.reason: Review finding 15: the pre-existing "releases all outputs when /RBO is driven LOW" case (wave2-combinational.test.ts) uses BCD=15, which LS47_SEGMENTS already decodes as fully blank — a core that ignored rbo_n entirely would pass it unnoticed. This case uses BCD=5 (a genuinely non-blank digit, the lamp-test case's own BCD), so releasing every segment here can only come from rbo_n's real precedence over the normal decode.

cases.name: control: the SAME BCD=5 with rbo_n HIGH (inactive) decodes normally — not every segment released
cases.reason: Control for the rbo_n-LOW case above: proves BCD=5 with rbo_n inactive is a genuinely non-blank pattern (at least one segment LOW), so the LOW-rbo_n case's "every segment released" is a real transition, not a circuit that reads all-released regardless of rbo_n.

cases.describe: gate 1 supplemental — 74HC14 Schmitt inverter: a genuinely observed propagation delay
cases.name: the digital commit lands measurably AFTER 1a crosses the Schmitt threshold — neither immediate (0ns) nor absurdly late (us-scale)
cases.reason: Review finding 15: the pre-existing 74hc14 prop_delay_ns=15 case (wave2-combinational.test.ts) loads with the input already at its final level, so its load-time settle (zero delay) resolves before any delay could be observed. A live RELOAD-based transition (the mechanism wave2-sequential.test.ts's 74HC74 edge tests use) is not usable either: a core reload re-runs decision 8's zero-delay t=0 settle with no per-id carry-forward yet (W2 scope — the same reason this file's own "Schmitt commit semantics"/prop_delay=35ns "not-yet" cases above are not portable), so the new input would commit with NO delay on the core only. This case instead feeds 1a from a plain RC network already present at load time — a genuine continuous analog crossing during ordinary step()s, with no second load() anywhere (the same mechanism fixture 19's relaxation oscillator uses) — and dynamically locates both the analog crossing and the digital commit, asserting the gap between them is bounded to the tens-of-ns ballpark the 15ns catalog value lives in, ruling out both "skipped entirely" and "some unrelated us-scale mechanism".

cases.describe: 74HC74 — D captured on rising edge only
cases.name: D=1 is captured when CLK goes LOW→HIGH (rising edge)
cases.reason: Verified by running against the core: passes. The circuit reloads once (CLK 0V->5V, D unchanged) after settling with CLK LOW for two steps. Before that reload the register is still at its power-on value (Q=0, core/README.md's "Register state" point 2), and the reload's own edge pass runs with lastClk forced to 0 (point 7: "The one edge pass then runs point 5 with every lastClk at 0"), so a clock already reading HIGH at reload is itself a rising edge -- classic's own phantom-edge behaviour, reproduced here. That phantom edge alone reconstructs Q=1 (D=1 captured) with no need to carry any pre-reload state forward, so the W2-scope load-carry-forward gap (no per-id state survives a core reload) is not observable in this specific case.

cases.describe: 74HC74 — D captured on rising edge only
cases.name: D=0 is captured when CLK goes LOW→HIGH
cases.reason: W2i: portable since W2c's load carry-forward (core/README.md, Carry). The reloads that move D and CLK carry the 74HC74's latch and its clock level, so a reload is no longer a phantom first observation and the flip-flop captures D only on the real rising edge. It failed before the carry (q1 read 0.031 V).

cases.describe: 74HC74 — D captured on rising edge only
cases.name: Q_n is always the complement of Q
cases.reason: Verified by running against the core: passes. Two independent SimEngine instances, each reloaded exactly ONCE (CLK 0V->5V) after a single settle with CLK LOW -- same phantom-edge reconstruction from power-on as the sibling "D=1 is captured" case (D=1 for engine1, D=0 for engine2), no cross-reload state hold asserted, so the load-carry-forward gap does not apply here either.

cases.describe: 74HC74 — D captured on rising edge only
cases.name: state holds with CLK high (no second capture)
cases.reason: W2i: portable since W2c's load carry-forward (core/README.md, Carry). Same carried latch and clock level as the 'D=0 is captured' sibling: the second reload changes D with CLK held high and Q does not move. It failed before the carry.

cases.name: /PRE LOW forces Q=1 regardless of CLK and D
cases.reason: Verified by running against the core: passes. Single load, no reload; /PRE is asynchronous and level-sensitive (core/README.md's sequential-ICs point 5), so this exercises real device behaviour with no load-carry-forward dependency at all.

cases.name: /CLR LOW forces Q=0 regardless of CLK and D
cases.reason: Verified by running against the core: passes. Single load, no reload; same reasoning as the sibling /PRE case.

cases.name: /CLR overrides a previously captured Q=1
cases.reason: Verified by running against the core: passes. Two reloads occur (capture D=1 via the same phantom-edge mechanism as "D=1 is captured", then assert /CLR LOW), but the SECOND reload's assertion depends only on /CLR being asserted -- point 5's asynchronous priority ("/clr 0 -> Q=0, Q1n=1") applies at every evaluation, including the frozen settle pass that runs before any edge (point 7: "the frozen settle drives classic's stamp view of the power-on state, with the live paths live... 74hc74 /pre and /clr"). So /CLR forces Q=0 regardless of whatever the register was reset to at reload -- the load-carry-forward gap is unobservable here because the assertion never depends on the PRE-reload state.

cases.name: both /PRE and /CLR LOW simultaneously: Q and Q_n BOTH HIGH (TI SN74HC74 SCLS108)
cases.reason: Verified by running against the core: passes. Single load, no reload; both overrides are asserted from t=0, exercised entirely through the frozen-settle async-priority path (point 5/7), no register-state dependency.

cases.name: releasing /CLR while /PRE stays asserted: Q_n goes LOW, Q stays HIGH
cases.reason: Verified by running against the core: passes. One reload occurs (release /CLR), but like the sibling "/CLR overrides" case the post-reload assertion depends only on /PRE staying LOW (forces Q=1, Q1n=0 at every evaluation, point 5's async priority), not on any state carried from before the reload -- the load-carry-forward gap is unobservable here too.

cases.name: outputs float when VCC is not connected
cases.reason: Verified by running against the core: passes. Single load, no reload, and no register-state dependency at all -- an unpowered IC drives nothing (core/README.md's W1c point 9, reused for sequential ICs by the sequential-ICs section's point 1), so the pull-up resistor alone sets the pin voltage.

cases.name: a rising edge on CLK counts up from power-on 0 to 1 (ENP=ENT=HIGH, /LOAD and /CLR inactive)
cases.reason: New case (this worker; core/README.md's sequential-ICs section, points 5-6). /CLR and /LOAD tied inactive HIGH, ENP=ENT=HIGH, CLK fed from a one-shot RC edge (1k/100pF, tau=100ns) that crosses the LS-TTL threshold within the 500ns step window -- a genuine analog clock edge inside a single load(), not a reload. Verified by running: count goes 0 -> 1 on the edge, and the bare digitalState count key ("the 161 publishes its count under the bare key <id>", README point 8) agrees with qa..qd.

cases.name: /CLR LOW holds the count at 0 across a clock edge that would otherwise count
cases.reason: New case (this worker). A=B=C=D tied to 15 (so a missed /CLR would show up immediately as a wrong parallel-load-shaped count) and the SAME RC clock edge as the sibling counting case genuinely crosses threshold, but /CLR is asynchronous and level-sensitive at every evaluation (README point 5), so the count never leaves 0. Verified by running: passes.

cases.name: control: RCO stays LOW at count 15 when ENT is LOW (RCO is gated by ENT, not just count==15)
cases.reason: New case (this worker); the control for the sibling RCO case -- same count=15 parallel load, ENT tied LOW instead of HIGH. Proves RCO genuinely depends on ENT and is not simply always HIGH once the count reaches 15 (the one row that would let a broken "RCO ignores ENT" implementation through the sibling case unnoticed). Verified by running: passes.

cases.name: a rising edge with G1=G2=LOW loads D1..D4 into Q1..Q4
cases.reason: New case (this worker; core/README.md's sequential-ICs section, 74ls173 row of points 5-6). /CLR tied inactive LOW (active-HIGH on this part), G1=G2=LOW, D1=1,D2=0,D3=1,D4=0, CLK from a one-shot RC edge. Verified by running: q1..q4 read 1,0,1,0 after the edge.

cases.name: M HIGH tri-states Q1 (a pull-up shows the float) while the register still holds the loaded D1=LOW
cases.reason: New case (this worker; README point 5, "M and N do not enter the update", and point 8, "the 173 shows its register while M or N tri-states the pins"). M tied HIGH throughout (so Q1 is HIZ from t=0), D1=LOW, G1=G2=LOW so the SAME clock edge that tri-states Q1 also loads D1 into the register underneath; a 10k pull-up to VCC on Q1 would read HIGH whether Q1 is genuinely floating or the pull-up is simply stronger than a driven LOW -- the point of this case is that a driven LOW output overpowers a 10k pull-up (as every other case in this file and combinational-ics.test.ts relies on), so reading Q1 HIGH here specifically shows Q1 is NOT driven, i.e. genuinely tri-stated. Verified by running: netVoltage(q1) > 4V (float, pulled up) while digitalState["u1/q1"] === 0 (the register's true, loaded content).

cases.name: the active-HIGH /CLR clears Q1..Q4 despite a load-triggering clock edge
cases.reason: New case (this worker). /CLR tied active HIGH throughout, D1..D4 all tied HIGH (would load 1111 if /CLR did not override), one RC clock edge. Verified by running: q1..q4 all read LOW after the edge -- /CLR's level override wins over the load, not merely "a load was never attempted".

cases.describe: gate 1 supplemental — 74HC74 divide-by-two from a live 74HC14 relaxation oscillator
cases.name: Q1_n -> D1 (toggle wiring): Q1 flips exactly once per oscillator rising edge, so Q1's own frequency is half the oscillator's
cases.reason: New case (this worker; the brief's "a free-running clock from fixture 19's 74hc14 relaxation oscillator"). The SAME R=10k/C=100nF Schmitt relaxation-oscillator topology as test/fixtures/core/19-74hc14-relaxation-oscillator.sim.json (built inline so its 1Y output can also drive u1.clk1), with Q1_n wired back to D1 (the classic toggle-flip-flop divide-by-two configuration) and /PRE1//CLR1 tied inactive HIGH. Verified by running for 3000 steps of 20us (60ms, several oscillator periods): the oscillator's own 1Y genuinely toggled more than 4 times, and Q1's own digitalState toggle count tracked the oscillator's rising-edge count 1:1 (within +/-1 for the run's start/end boundary) -- a D=Q_bar flip-flop flips its OWN state on every rising clock edge, so its OWN PERIOD (not its toggle count) is twice the clock's, the textbook divide-by-two.

cases.describe: gate 1 supplemental — 74HC74 divide-by-two from a live 74HC14 relaxation oscillator
cases.name: /PRE1 LOW holds Q1 HIGH the whole time, despite a running clock
cases.reason: New case (this worker). Same live oscillator driving clk1 as the sibling toggle case, but /PRE1 tied LOW (asserted) for the whole run and D1 tied to a defined LOW instead of the toggle feedback. Verified by running for 3000 steps: digitalState["u1/q1"]===1 and ["u1/q1_n"]===0 at every single sampled step -- a genuinely live, oscillating clock never manages to flip Q1, proving /PRE1 is a real asynchronous override and not merely "the clock never toggled".

cases.describe: gate 1 supplemental — 74HC74 divide-by-two from a live 74HC14 relaxation oscillator
cases.name: /CLR1 LOW holds Q1 LOW the whole time, despite a running clock
cases.reason: New case (this worker); the /CLR1 mirror of the sibling /PRE1 case, same reasoning and same verification (Q1 stays 0 / Q1_n stays 1 at every one of 3000 sampled steps).

cases.name: power-on: mem[addr]=0xF reads back inverted -- /O1../O4 all LOW -- while /CS is LOW and /WE is HIGH
cases.reason: New case (this worker; core/README.md's memories section, 74ls189 State-at-load and Publish points). /CS tied active LOW, /WE tied inactive HIGH, address tied to 0, a 10k pull-up per output pin (so a driven LOW is distinguishable from a floating HIGH). Verified by running: /O1../O4 all read LOW, matching the power-on mem=0xF inverted through all four bits.

cases.name: a write through /WE (driven low-to-high by an RC edge) stores D1..D4, then a read shows the new nibble inverted
cases.reason: New case (this worker; the brief's own 74ls189 write case). /CS tied active LOW throughout; address tied to 5 and D1..D4 tied to nibble 6 (0b0110) throughout; /WE fed from a one-shot RC edge starting LOW (the capacitor is uncharged at a fresh load, same fact combinational-ics.test.ts's own 74HC14 case relies on) and rising to HIGH. Per README's 74ls189 write rule ("Write, with edges live only: when csLow && weHigh && lastWE==0, mem[addr]=D... the trailing edge of /we"): /we reads LOW at the load settle, so lastWE settles to 0 there (no phantom write, matching "State at load"'s own no-phantom-write guarantee); the RC node's later LOW->HIGH crossing is then exactly the trailing edge the rule keys on, with the address/data lines already at their final (static) values. Verified by running: after the edge, /O1=HIGH (d1=0), /O2=LOW (d2=1), /O3=LOW (d3=1), /O4=HIGH (d4=0) -- the new nibble, inverted.

cases.describe: gate 1 supplemental — 28C16 EEPROM: a static read of a known byte
cases.name: /OE and /CE LOW, /WE HIGH: IO0..IO7 read back the seeded byte 0x5A at the tied address
cases.reason: New case (this worker; the brief's "a read of a known byte from params.contents at a tied address" -- the write path is D4b's harness job, needing switch stimuli). /OE and /CE tied active LOW, /WE tied inactive HIGH (pure read, no write ever attempted), address tied to 0x100, params.contents base64-encodes a 2048-byte image that is 0xFF everywhere except byte 0x100 = 0x5A. A fully static circuit -- no reload, no live param, no RC edge needed at all for a plain read. Verified by running: IO0..IO7 read back 0x5A's bits exactly (both via getNetV and digitalState).

cases.describe: gate 1 supplemental — 28C256 EEPROM: a static read of a known byte
cases.name: /OE and /CE LOW, /WE HIGH: IO0..IO7 read back the seeded byte 0xC3 at the tied address
cases.reason: New case (this worker). Same mechanism as the 28C16 read case, one address-bit family wider (a0..a14, 15 bits, size 32768) -- needed because gate-reporter.ts's coverage-floor check (finding 9) counts "28c16" and "28c256" as two separate CORE_IMPLEMENTED_KINDS entries, so the 28C16 case alone would leave 28c256 at zero. Address 0x4321, seeded byte 0xC3. Verified by running: IO0..IO7 read back 0xC3's bits exactly.

cases.name: seg7_cc rejects conflicting voltages on its duplicate COM leads
cases.reason: graph.ts bonds COM and COM2 into one net, so the ideal source wired across them has both terminals on one net: a loop of ideal sources, which the core rejects as a topology decline (-3, 'topology:voltage_source (component 1): both terminals already fixed') and HeadlessRunner falls back to classic for. The adapter's load() then throws CoreSuiteFellBackError by design. The case asserts classic's own lastConverged === false for that circuit, which has no core counterpart (same shape as high-impedance's conflicting-source cases).

cases.name: unconnected segments report ~0 current

cases.name: a seg7_cc with no pins wired has zero channel current
cases.reason: Stays not-yet: the assertion sits inside `if (ch !== undefined)` and the case's own comment accepts 'absent or all zeros', so it pins no behaviour. With the delegating adapter the guard is entered and eight zero slots are checked, but with no pin wired there is no junction that could conduct; a core (or a stub) publishing nothing would satisfy it just as well. Not counted as coverage.

cases.name: reverse polarity (CC wired as CA) produces near-zero current

Failed while the adapter stubbed getElementChannelI() as {}; ran and passed on the core once the adapter delegated it to the active readout (W1e follow-up).

cases.name: records the state on both sides of each 555 switch, inside the step that switched
cases.reason: Classic-only by ruling D18 (a), W2 design section 5: step breakpoints are not ported. They record classic's state on both sides of a 555 switch inside the fixed step that contained it; the core has no fixed step to split (it lands on the 555's commit instant exactly) and CoreEngine has no takeStepBreakpoints. What the breakpoints were for, the light and the waveform between samples, is the core's acquisition and charge (core/README.md, Acquisition and Charge), which gate 2 covers.

cases.name: shows the preloaded word at every address, inverted on the /O pins
cases.reason: New file (RAM preload, coordinator ruling 2026-11-13; core/README.md memories point 2a). Sixteen loads, one per tied address, /WE tied HIGH: the core reads the preload from the record's blob tail at load, with no seed call. Verified by running on both engines.

cases.name: with no contents every address reads the blank word 0xF, as before the field existed
cases.reason: Pins memories point 2 for a record with no preload (blob of 15 values). Passes on both engines before and after the preload landed.

cases.name: reads contents that are not base64 as the blank word
cases.reason: The compiler carries classic's own decode (ramPreloadWords), so a value atob refuses is sixteen 0xF nibbles on both engines.

cases.describe: 74LS189 preload: a write, then a read
cases.name: a write replaces the preloaded word at its address
cases.reason: /WE from a one-shot RC edge inside one load (the mechanism sequential-memory-ics.test.ts uses): the trailing edge writes D over the preloaded word.

cases.name: restores the preload and drops the write
cases.reason: The chip's own supply is a voltage_source whose live `voltage` the case edits in place (5 -> 0 -> 5); the adapter delivers it through setParams, as eeprom-write.test.ts's edits. The core's event evaluates the 189 unpowered with edges live, which is where the preload returns (memories point 2a).

cases.name: with no contents the written word is still there after the same outage, as before the field existed
cases.reason: Pins sequential point 3 for a 189 with no preload: its state freezes through an outage on both engines. Passes before and after the preload landed.

cases.name: a blank preload (contents that are not base64) comes back as 0xF after an outage
cases.reason: The blank image is a preload like any other on both engines.

cases.name: a supply that sags to 3 V and recovers is a power loss too
cases.reason: The chip's supply is a one-shot pulse_source ramping 5 V -> 3 V -> 5 V inside one load: the core sees the outage through the ramp's own events on a fixed node, with no setParams. 3 V is under the power window (0.9 x vccMin).

cases.name: a reload that leaves the chip alone keeps the live word, not the preload
cases.reason: A second load() of an edited copy (one pull-up's resistance): W2c's carry seeds the 189's words before the settle, whose frozen first pass reads every IC unpowered; that pass is not a power loss (memories point 2a), so the written word survives.

cases.name: a reload with other contents starts from them
cases.reason: mapCarry drops a RAM's IC record onto another preload, as classic's load() starts the chip from its new contents.

cases.describe: 74LS189 with no contents: classic's state is untouched
cases.name: keeps exactly the slots it had before the field existed
cases.reason: Reads classic's icState slot names through getIcState; the core keeps the 189's words in its evaluator, with no such record.
